readings.title: The Vision of the Locusts
readings.subtitle: Amos Intercedes for Israel
readings.text:
[Amos 7:1] This is what the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> showed me, and see, <dn>He</dn> was forming locust swarms at the beginning of the late crop. And see, it was the late crop after the mowings of the sovereign.
[2] And it came to be, when they had finished eating <dn>את</dn> the grass of the land, that <dn>I</dn> said, “O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, forgive, <dn>I</dn> pray! How does Ya‛aqoḇ survive, for he is small?”
[3] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> relented concerning this. <dq>“It shall not be,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Vision of the Fire
readings.subtitle: Amos Intercedes Again
readings.text:
[Amos 7:4] This is what the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> showed me, and see, the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was calling to contend by fire, and it consumed <dn>את</dn> the great deep and did consume <dn>את</dn> the portion,
[5] and <dn>I</dn> said, “O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, please stop! How does Ya‛aqoḇ survive, for he is small?”
[6] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> relented concerning this. <dq>“This shall not be either,”</dq> said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Vision of the Plumb-line
readings.subtitle: The Lord's Unwavering Standard
readings.text:
[Amos 7:7] This is what <dn>He</dn> showed me, and see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stood on a wall made with a plumb-line, with a plumb-line in <dn>His</dn> hand,
[8] and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“Amos, what do you see?”</dq> And <dn>I</dn> said, “A plumb-line.” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am setting <dn>את</dn> a plumb-line in the midst of <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl, no longer do <dn>I</dn> pardon them.</dq>
[9] <dq>“And the high places of Yitsḥaq shall be laid waste, and the set-apart places of Yisra’ěl shall be destroyed. And <dn>I</dn> shall rise with the sword against the house of Yaroḇ‛am.”</dq>

readings.title: Amos and Amaziah
readings.subtitle: The Prophet Confronts the Priest of Bethel
readings.text:
[Amos 7:10] Then Amatsyah the priest of Běyth Ěl sent to Yaroḇ‛am sovereign of Yisra’ěl, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Yisra’ěl. The land is not able to endure all his words,
[11] for this is what Amos said, ‘Yaroḇ‛am shall die by the sword, and Yisra’ěl certainly be exiled from their own land.’ ”
[12] And Amatsyah said to Amos, “Go, you seer! Flee to the land of Yehuḏah, and eat bread and prophesy there,
[13] but do not prophesy any more at Běyth Ěl, for it is the sovereign’s set-apart place and it is the house of the reign.”
[14] And Amos answered and said to Amatsyah, “<dn>I</dn> am not a prophet, nor am <dn>I</dn> a son of a prophet, for <dn>I</dn> am a herdsman and a grower of sycamore figs.
[15] “But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> took me from behind the flock, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Go, prophesy to <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl.’</dq>
[16] “And now, hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. You are saying, ‘Do not prophesy against Yisra’ěl, and do not drop words against the house of Yitsḥaq.’
[17] “Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Your wife shall become a whore in the city, and your sons and daughters fall by the sword, and your land be divided by a measuring line, and you die in a defiled land, and Yisra’ěl shall certainly be exiled from its land.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Vision of Summer Fruit
readings.subtitle: The End Has Come for Israel
readings.text:
[Amos 8:1] This is what the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> showed me, and see, a basket of summer fruit.
[2] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Amos, what do you see?”</dq> And <dn>I</dn> said, “A basket of summer fruit.” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“The end has come upon <dn>my</dn> people Yisra’ěl, no longer do <dn>I</dn> pardon them.</dq>
[3] <dq>“And the songs of the Hěḵal shall be wailing in that day,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“many dead bodies everywhere, thrown into any place – hush!”</dq>

readings.title: Judgment on the Oppressors
readings.subtitle: Woe to Those Who Exploit the Poor
readings.text:
[Amos 8:4] Hear this, you who are swallowing up the needy, to do away with the poor of the land,
[5] saying, “When does the New moon pass so that we sell grain, and the Sabbath so that we trade our wheat, to make the ěphah small and the sheqel large, and to falsify the scales by deceit,
[6] to buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals, and sell the chaff of the wheat?”
[7] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sworn by the Excellency of Ya‛aqoḇ, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall never forget any of their works.</dq>
[8] <dq>“Shall the land not tremble for this, and everyone mourn who dwells in it? And all of it shall swell like the River, heave and subside like the River of Mitsrayim.</dq>
[9] <dq>“And it shall be in that day,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that <dn>I</dn> shall cause the sun to go down at noon, and shall darken <dn>את</dn> the earth on a day of brightness,</dq>
[10] <dq>and shall turn your festivals into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation, and bring sackcloth on all loins, and baldness on every head, and shall make it like mourning for an only son, and its end like a day of bitterness.</dq>

readings.title: A Famine for the Word
readings.subtitle: Israel Will Seek but Not Find
readings.text:
[Amos 8:11] <dq>“See, days are coming,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that <dn>I</dn> shall send a hunger in the land, not a hunger for bread, nor a thirst for water, but for hearing <dn>את</dn> the Words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[12] <dq>“And they shall wander from sea to sea, and from north to east – they shall diligently search, seeking <dn>את</dn> the Word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but they shall not find it.</dq>
[13] <dq>“In that day the beautiful maidens and strong young men shall faint from thirst,</dq>
[14] <dq>those swearing by the guilt of Shomeron, who say, ‘As your mighty one lives, O Dan!’ and, ‘As the way of Be’ěrsheḇa lives!’ And they shall fall and never rise again.”</dq>

readings.title: Vision of Judgment at the Altar
readings.subtitle: No Escape for the Wicked
readings.text:
[Amos 9:1] <dn>I</dn> saw <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> standing by the slaughter-place, and <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Strike <dn>את</dn> the column head, so that the thresholds shake, and break them off by the head, all of them. And <dn>את</dn> the last of them <dn>I</dn> kill with the sword. Not one of them fleeing gets away, and not one fugitive of them escapes.</dq>
[2] <dq>“If they dig into She’ol, from there <dn>my</dn> hand does take them; and if they climb up to the heavens, from there <dn>I</dn> bring them down.</dq>
[3] <dq>“And if they hide themselves on top of Karmel, from there <dn>I</dn> shall search, and take them. And if they hide from before <dn>My</dn> eyes at the bottom of the sea, from there <dn>I</dn> shall command <dn>את</dn> the serpent, and it shall bite them.</dq>
[4] <dq>“And if they go into captivity before their enemies, from there <dn>I</dn> shall command <dn>את</dn> the sword, and it shall kill them. And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> eyes on them for evil and not for good.”</dq>
[5] And the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is <dn>He</dn> who touches the earth so that it melts, and all who dwell in it mourn, and all of it come up like the River, and subside like the River of Mitsrayim –
[6] who is building <dn>His</dn> upper room in the heavens, and has founded <dn>His</dn> firmament on the earth, who is calling for the waters of the sea, and pours them out on the face of the earth – <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>His</dn> Name.

readings.title: Israel Judged Like Other Nations
readings.subtitle: The Sinful Kingdom Destroyed, A Remnant Spared
readings.text:
[Amos 9:7] <dq>“Are you not like the people of Kush to <dn>Me</dn>, O children of Yisra’ěl?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Did <dn>I</dn> not bring up <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from the land of Mitsrayim, and <dn>את</dn> the Philistines from Kaphtor, and <dn>את</dn> Aram from Qir?</dq>
[8] <dq>“Look, the eyes of the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> are on the sinful reign, and <dn>I</dn> shall destroy it from the face of the earth, except that, <dn>I</dn> do not completely destroy <dn>את</dn> the house of Ya‛aqoḇ,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[9] <dq>“For look, <dn>I</dn> am commanding, and <dn>I</dn> shall sift <dn>את</dn> the house of Yisra’ěl among all the nations, as one sifts with a sieve, yet not a grain falls to the ground.</dq>
[10] <dq>“All the sinners of <dn>My</dn> people are going to die by the sword, those who are saying, ‘Evil does not overtake us nor meet us.’</dq>

readings.title: The Promise of Restoration
readings.subtitle: The Booth of David Rebuilt
readings.text:
[Amos 9:11] <dq>“In that day <dn>I</dn> shall raise up <dn>את</dn> the Booth of Daviḏ which has fallen down. And <dn>I</dn> shall repair its breaches and raise up its ruins. And <dn>I</dn> shall build it as in the days of old,</dq>
[12] <dq>so that they possess <dn>את</dn> the remnant of Eḏom, and <dn>את</dn> all the nations on whom <dn>My</dn> Name is called,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who does this.
[13] <dq>“Look, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that the ploughman shall overtake <dn>את</dn> the reaper, and the treader of grapes him who sows seed. And the mountains shall drip new wine, and all the hills melt.</dq>
[14] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall turn back <dn>את</dn> the captivity of <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl. And they shall build the waste cities and inhabit them. And they shall plant vineyards and drink wine from them, and shall make gardens and eat their fruit.</dq>
[15] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall plant them on their own soil, and not uproot them any more from their own soil <dn>I</dn> have given them,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>!

readings.subsection: The Decline of Israel and Judah
readings.title: The End of Jeroboam II's Reign
readings.subtitle: His Acts and Death
readings.text:
[2 Kings 14:28] And the rest of the acts of Yaroḇ‛am, and all that he did, and his might, how he fought, and how he recovered Dammeseq and Ḥamath for Yehuḏah in Yisra’ěl, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl?
[29] So Yaroḇ‛am slept with his fathers, the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl. And Zeḵaryah his son reigned in his place.

readings.subsection: The Decline of Israel and Judah
readings.title: The Reign and Assassination of Zechariah
readings.subtitle: The Word to Jehu is Fulfilled
readings.text:
[2 Kings 15:8] In the thirty-eighth year of Azaryahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, Zeḵaryahu son of Yaroḇ‛am began to reign over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron, for six new moons.
[9] And he did <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as his fathers had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ěl sin.
[10] And Shallum son of Yaḇěsh conspired against him, and struck him in front of the people, and killed him, and reigned in his place.
[11] And the rest of the acts of Zeḵaryah, see, they are written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl.
[12] This was the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> spoke to Yěhu, saying, <dq>“Your sons to the fourth generation are going to sit on the throne of Yisra’ěl.”</dq> And it came to be so.

readings.subsection: The Decline of Israel and Judah
readings.title: The Reign and Assassination of Shallum
readings.subtitle: A One-Month Reign
readings.text:
[2 Kings 15:13] Shallum son of Yaḇěsh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziyah, the sovereign of Yehuḏah. And he reigned a month of days in Shomeron.
[14] And Menaḥěm son of Gaḏi went up from Tirtsah, and came to Shomeron, and struck Shallum son of Yaḇěsh in Shomeron and killed him, and reigned in his place.
[15] And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy which he led, see, they are written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl.

readings.subsection: The Decline of Israel and Judah
readings.title: The Reign of Menahem
readings.subtitle: Tribute to Assyria
readings.text:
[2 Kings 15:16] And Menaḥěm struck Tiphsaḥ, and all who were there, and its borders, from Tirtsah. Because they did not open it to him, therefore he struck it. And he ripped open all the pregnant women.
[17] In the thirty-ninth year of Azaryah sovereign of Yehuḏah, Menaḥěm son of Gaḏi began to reign over Yisra’ěl, ten years in Shomeron.
[18] And he did <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. He did not turn away from the sins of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ěl sin, all his days.
[19] Pul the sovereign of Ashshur came against the land. And Menaḥěm gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, for his hand to be with him to strengthen the reign in his hand.
[20] And Menaḥěm exacted <dn>את</dn> the silver of Yisra’ěl, of all the mighty men of wealth, of each man fifty sheqels of silver, to give to the sovereign of Ashshur. And the sovereign of Ashshur turned back, and did not stay there in the land.

readings.subsection: The Decline of Israel and Judah
readings.title: The End of Menahem's Reign
readings.subtitle: Pekahiah Succeeds Him
readings.text:
[2 Kings 15:21] And the rest of the acts of Menaḥěm, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl?
[22] So Menaḥěm slept with his fathers. And Peqaḥyah his son reigned in his place.

readings.subsection: The Decline of Israel and Judah
readings.title: The Reign and Assassination of Pekahiah
readings.subtitle: Conspiracy by Pekah
readings.text:
[2 Kings 15:23] In the fiftieth year of Azaryah the sovereign of Yehuḏah, Peqaḥyah the son of Menaḥěm began to reign over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron, for two years.
[24] And he did <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. He did not turn away from the sins of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ěl sin.
[25] And Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, a chief officer of his, conspired against him and struck him in Shomeron, in the high place of the sovereign’s house, along with Argoḇ and Aryěh, and with him were fifty men of Gil‛aḏ. So he killed him and reigned in his place.
[26] And the rest of the acts of Peqaḥyah, and all that he did, see, they are written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl.

readings.subsection: The Decline of Israel and Judah
readings.title: The Reign of Pekah
readings.subtitle: The Assyrian Invasion
readings.text:
[2 Kings 15:27] In the fifty-second year of Azaryah sovereign of Yehuḏah, Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu began to reign over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron, for twenty years.
[28] And he did <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. He did not turn away from the sins of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ěl sin.
[29] In the days of Peqaḥ sovereign of Yisra’ěl, Tiḡlath-Pileser sovereign of Ashshur came and took <dn>את</dn> Iyon, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇěl Běyth Ma‛aḵah, and <dn>את</dn> Yanovaḥ, and <dn>את</dn> Qeḏesh, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥatsor, and <dn>את</dn> Gil‛aḏ, and <dn>את</dn> Galil, all <dn>את</dn> the land of Naphtali, and took them into exile to Ashshur.

readings.subsection: The Decline of Israel and Judah
readings.title: The End of Azariah's Reign
readings.subtitle: Jotham Succeeds Him
readings.text:
[2 Kings 15:6] And the rest of the acts of Azaryahu, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah?
[7] So Azaryah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the City of Daviḏ. And Yotham his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: Isaiah's Vision of the Lord
readings.subtitle: In the Year King Uzziah Died
readings.text:
[Isaiah 6:1] In the year that Sovereign Uzziyahu died, <dn>I</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and the train of <dn>His</dn> robe filled the Hěḵal.
[2] Above it stood seraphim. Each one had six wings: with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.
[3] And one cried to another and said, “Set-apart, set-apart, set-apart is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts; all the earth is filled with <dn>His</dn> esteem!”
[4] And the posts of the door were shaken by the voice of him who cried out, and the house was filled with smoke.

readings.title: Isaiah's Cleansing
readings.subtitle: A Live Coal from the Altar
readings.text:
[Isaiah 6:5] And <dn>I</dn> said, “Woe to me, for <dn>I</dn> am undone! Because <dn>I</dn> am a man of unclean lips, and <dn>I</dn> dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips – for my eyes have seen <dn>את</dn> the Sovereign, <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.”
[6] And one of the seraphim flew to me, having in his hand a live coal which he had taken with the tongs from the slaughter-place.
[7] And he touched my mouth with it, and said, “See, this has touched your lips; your crookedness is taken away, and your sin is covered.”

readings.title: Isaiah's Commission
readings.subtitle: A Message of Judgment and Hope
readings.text:
[Isaiah 6:8] And <dn>I</dn> heard <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, <dq>“Whom do <dn>I</dn> send, and who would go for <dn>Us</dn>?”</dq> And <dn>I</dn> said, “Here am <dn>I</dn>! Send me.”
[9] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Go, and you shall say to this people, ‘Hearing, you hear, but do not understand; and seeing, you see, but do not know.’</dq>
[10] <dq>“Make <dn>את</dn> the heart of this people fat, and their ears heavy, and shut <dn>את</dn> their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and shall turn and be healed.”</dq>
[11] Then <dn>I</dn> said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, until when?” And <dn>He</dn> answered, <dq>“Until the cities are laid waste and without inhabitant, and the houses are without a man, and the land is laid waste, a ruin,</dq>
[12] <dq>and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has removed <dn>את</dn> men far away, and the forsaken places be many in the midst of the land.</dq>
[13] <dq>“But still, there is a tenth part in it, and it shall again be for a burning, like a terebinth tree and like an oak, whose stump remains when it is cut down. The set-apart seed is its stump!”</dq>
